c.tagline: Scottish-founded city of Victorian grandeur, students and wild Otago coast.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered; Dunedin Taxis and Southern Taxis are the main operators, and Uber also operates in the city.

emergency.note: 111 is the single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance across New Zealand; Dunedin Hospital runs the main public emergency department.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Rowdy student parties around North Dunedin's Castle Street on big weekends; otherwise usual awareness.

hood_desc: The civic heart around the eight-sided Octagon plaza, ringed by the Dunedin Railway Station, cafes, bars and galleries; the most central, walkable base for first-time visitors.
The lively student quarter around the University of Otago's bluestone campus and North East Valley, full of cheap eats, flats and pubs; suits younger travellers and a budget stay near the action.
Dunedin's seaside suburbs on a long surf beach, with the St Clair saltwater pool, esplanade cafes and coastal walks; a relaxed, scenic base for those wanting the coast over the city.
A revived heritage precinct of Victorian warehouses on Vogel and lower Stuart Streets, now home to design studios, craft coffee, street art and small bars; best for a creative, indie vibe.
A historic deep-water port village about 15 km from the centre, with steep streets, galleries, seafood and cruise-ship bustle; a quiet, artsy escape with harbour views.
lodging: Majestic Mansions Apartments at St Clair

water.note: Tap water is safe and excellent quality.

transit.hours: Orbus buses run roughly 7am to around 11pm on weekdays with reduced weekend and evening services; there is no rail or night network, so taxis and Uber cover late hours.
transit.note: Dunedin's public transport is the Orbus bus network run by the Otago Regional Council; there are no trains or trams, and the compact city centre is easily walked.
transit.pay: Tap on and off with a prepaid Bee Card (sold at the bus hub and retailers) for the cheapest fares, or pay the driver with cash; contactless bank-card payment is also accepted on board.

bus: InterCity coach services to Christchurch, Queenstown and Invercargill
Atomic Travel and other regional coaches
train: Dunedin Railways scenic excursions (Taieri Gorge / Seasider) — tourist services only, no scheduled passenger rail

transit.m: Super Shuttle door-to-door shared van to the city centre (~30-40 min)
Private airport transfer / coach connection to central Dunedin

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in New Zealand; rounding up or leaving ~10% for exceptional service is appreciated but never expected.
